wiki_text: Kerawalapitiya has passed through several sponsors. India's Petronet LNG and Japanese partners (Mitsubishi/Sojitz) first proposed a ~$250m, 2.6-2.7 mtpa import terminal in 2017 (sundaytimes.lk, upstreamonline.com), targeting a 2021 start. Sri Lanka's government cancelled the Petronet deal in Aug 2022 for lack of progress and re-tendered; the tender was subsequently reported won by China Harbour Engineering Co Ltd (CHEC), initially in a consortium with Pakistan's Engro Corp. Petronet re-emerged in a 2024 government-to-government LNG SUPPLY arrangement (separate from the terminal-development tender) covering interim gas to the Kerawalapitiya power complex pending the new terminal (sundaytimes.lk/240728, sundaytimes.lk/240714). In Aug 2025, Sri Lanka formally awarded the FSRU + pipeline project (Build-Own-Operate-Transfer) to CHEC, after Engro withdrew from the consortium and CHEC committed to naming a replacement partner (ceylontoday.lk 2025-08-02 -- see qa note on this ref's automated-verification status). In Feb 2026, Sri Lanka and India (via Petronet) signed a further MoU specifically for LNG infrastructure/supply to the adjacent 'Sobadhanavi' combined-cycle power plant at Kerawalapitiya (ft.lk/44-765800) -- an interim/parallel gas-SUPPLY arrangement to the existing Kerawalapitiya power stations while the CHEC-led terminal is built, not a reversal of the CHEC terminal award. Sobadhanavi's initial LNG supply reportedly moves via ISO container from Petronet's Kochi (India) terminal by ship to Colombo Port, then by truck to Kerawalapitiya -- a small-scale interim logistics chain tied to the SAME Kerawalapitiya site/project already tracked here, not a separate in-scope terminal.
